decisions.quote: In the Croninger et al. (2007) study, the authors found that important teacher-level characteristics for achievement include having an elementary education degree. Teacher characteristics aggregated to the school level, such as the average number of courses teachers have taken in reading or having a high number of teachers with advanced degrees, are related to reading and mathematics achievement. Similar to the Croninger et al. (2007) study, the aggregate average of teachers who have had a reading course did positively relate to reading achievement, but no other teacher characteristics were statistically significant.
decisions.reason: When comparing their results to Croninger et al. (2007), the authors explicitly report that the school-aggregated reading coursework association agreed with the original study while the other previously significant teacher-characteristic effects did not replicate, making the outcome mixed rather than failed.
